title: Introduce queue-cutoff and burst concurrency shaper for dedicated fleets
author: Jordan Patel
release_notes: Added two capacity controls for Dedicated fleets: a queue-cutoff mechanism to bound long-tail queuing under overload, and a burst concurrency shaper that maintains tenant throughput guarantees during short bursts. Configurable via fleet policy and feature-flagged for incremental rollout.
description:
Summary:
This PR introduces two complementary controls for Dedicated capacity: (1) queue-cutoff, a lightweight admission policy that drops or downgrades low-priority requests when queue depth exceeds a tenant-specific cutoff to prevent head-of-line amplification and p99+ latency cliffs; and (2) burst concurrency shaper, which enforces a short-window concurrency envelope for bursts while preserving committed throughput by distributing excess concurrency across warm slots and tracked credits.

Motivation and context:
We saw several production incidents where tail queuing during short multi-tenant spikes caused disproportionate p95/p99 regressions and SLA breaches for committed tenants. Existing backpressure (gateway backoffs + fair-scheduler) mitigates long-term overload but fails to prevent immediate headroom exhaustion that creates long queue tails. This change targets that immediate timescale and aims to keep committed throughput stable during bursts while giving low-priority traffic a bounded failure mode (cutoff) instead of long waits.

Design (high level):
- queue-cutoff: per-tenant sliding window that tracks outstanding queue length and per-req priority score. When outstanding > cutoff_threshold, new low-priority requests are either rejected with 429, retried-as-background, or redirected based on tenant policy. Cutoff_threshold is derived from tenant reservation, configured minimum concurrency, and observed service time distribution.
- burst concurrency shaper: short (configurable, default 5s) moving-window scheduler that caps the instantaneous concurrency assigned to non-committed burst requests. When bursts exceed headroom, the shaper uses a credit-pool to amortize excess work across warm slots (soft-spillover) and marks requests for graceful degradation if credits are exhausted.
- Telemetry: new metrics registered: dedicated.queue_cutoff_invocations, dedicated.queue_cutoff_reject_rate, dedicated.burst_shaper_applied, dedicated.burst_shaper_credit_balance, and dedicated.tenant_burst_headroom_ms. Dashboards updated and alert thresholds added for excessive cutoff invocations.
- Config and flags: feature gate enable_queue_cutoff_v2; fleet policy fields: cutoff.policy (reject|background|redirect), cutoff.window_ms, shaper.window_s, shaper.base_capacity_pct, shaper.credit_decay_ms.

Changed areas and notable code paths:
- pkg/autoscaler/cutoff.go: new implementation of sliding-window cutoff and admission policy hooks into request admission path.
- pkg/autoscaler/shaper.go: implements the burst concurrency window, credit accounting, and warm-slot spillover logic.
- cmd/agent/config.go + deploy/helm/values.dedicated.yaml: added knobs and defaults for Dedicated fleets; documented safe defaults.
- telemetry and observability: metric registration + dashboard json for SRE + product monitoring.
- tests: unit tests for cutoff decision boundaries, e2e that simulates multi-tenant bursts and asserts committed-tenant p99 improvement. Perf bench included to exercise shaper under high fan-in.

Performance and test results:
- Local perf bench (simulated 100 tenants, 12 committed heavy tenants, 88 opportunistic): under a synthetic 10x burst, p95 for committed tenants dropped from 220ms to 78ms, p99 from 680ms to 210ms, and SLA-compliant request fraction increased by ~9 percentage points.
- Integration e2e (staging): cutoff_invocation rate observed during a replay of incident load was ~0.8% of total requests; most were low-priority background requests and were retried by caller. No data plane errors for committed tenants were observed.
- Unit tests: cutoff edge cases, shaper credit underflow/overflow, config validation. CI added a small synthetic stress test as part of the pre-merge suite.

Rollout and safety plan:
- Feature gated behind enable_queue_cutoff_v2 and rollout coordinate: start with conservative defaults and opt-in for a subset of Dedicated pools via fleet policy.
- Canary steps: enable on 5% of fleet small pools -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% while monitoring dedicated.burst_shaper_credit_balance and dedicated.queue_cutoff_reject_rate.
- On high rejection rates, policy can be switched to background mode to avoid immediate client-visible 429s.

Review convo (high-level transcript):
- Ava: "Design looks reasonable. Need strong justifications for default cutoff thresholds and safe-mode behavior if credit accounting fails."
- Author: "Added a conservative formula in config.go (cutoff = max(4, min(0.2*reservation_rps, 32))) and a fallback that disables shaper and sets cutoff to high-water mark if any accounting panic occurs. Post-merge we can tune defaults based on canary telemetry."
- Liam: "Consider exposing a tenant-visible header when requests are cutoff so clients can retry or downgrade gracefully."
- Author: "Added: X-Redwood-Cutoff: reason=queue_limit; ttl=30s"
- Priya: "Can we guarantee no additional memory retention for KV cache?"
- Author: "No changes to KV cache lifecycle; shaper only interacts with admission and a small credit counter per tenant (bounded). Unit tests assert no leak over long runs."
- Ava: "Approve after small nits addressed and an observability playbook snippet."

CI and merge steps:
- CI pipeline: unit -> linters -> integration-e2e -> perf-smoke -> deploy-canary. One flaky perf job retried once; all checks passed on final run.
- Merge method: squash merge to keep history compact. Changelog entry added.

Post-merge tasks (short):
- Monitor dedicated.queue_cutoff_reject_rate and dedicated.burst_shaper_credit_balance for the first 72 hours after canary enablement.
- Run a follow-up to add an opt-in tenant dashboard with top offenders and a suggested policy (ENG-9103).

Commits (summary):
- "feat(autoscaler): add burst concurrency shaper and credit accounting"
- "feat(autoscaler): add queue cutoff admission policy and hooks"
- "chore(config): add dedicated fleet knobs and feature flag"
- "test(e2e): add staged burst replay and assertion harness"
- "docs: document cutoff/shaper tuning guide for Dedicated"

Merge outcome:
- Approved by reviewers Ava Martinez and Priya Singh; minor nits addressed. CI green on final run. Merged via squash.

Notes for SRE and support:
- There is a new optional alert: Alert if dedicated.queue_cutoff_reject_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m on production fleets with committed tenants.
- If customers report increased 429s after enabling, switch their fleet policy cutoff.policy from reject->background and escalate to platform-engineering for tuning.
notes_for_oncall: New metric alerts: dedicated.queue_cutoff_reject_rate and dedicated.burst_shaper_credit_balance. Default cutoff is conservative; if customers see elevated 429s during canary, flip policy to background and open ENG-9103 for tuning.
changelog_entry: Added queue-cutoff admission policy and burst concurrency shaper for Dedicated fleets (feature-flagged). Improves committed-tenant latency under short bursts and provides configurable failure modes for low-priority traffic.
